sources.note: Live main at product session takeover; newer than the 2026-09-03 handoff snapshot 10567c22.
Previous product session closeout; re-verified against live GitHub, not trusted verbatim.
Terra slot 1: block-times page wired to the existing /api/block-times endpoints.
Terra slot 2: trip plan display ordering exposed in the guide UI; trip_plans.sort_order already exists.

notes: Product delivery session resumed after the previous session left ACTIVE product PRs at zero following the #162 merge.
Free dual-Terra pilot: slot 1 Issue #7 block-times wiring, slot 2 Issue #42 plan display ordering; no file overlap and no migration in either lane.
Governance work (#163/#164) is handled by a separate session and is not claimed here.
No completion, remote canonical TEST, merge or Issue-close claim is made at initialization.

Main advanced to 549402f471ffd4786a44319ca5bc169f897ce67e (governance #164) during triage; #164 touched only workflows, agent scripts, docs and governance tests, so no product source rebuild was required and both Terra branches are based on 549402f.

Owner steer 2026-09-04: restore broken features rather than removing them. PR #169 was re-scoped from a field-removal to a full restore (title/recurrence/full_day/auto + PUT endpoint + WEEKLY expansion in availability and calendar).

Sol audit caught two fake-success defects that exact-head CI had passed: PR #168 sortOrder tie values (seed rows share the default 0, so a reorder wrote 0 back and changed nothing while showing a success toast) and PR #169 mock-mode create that never persisted.

GOVERNANCE_FOLLOWUP: block_times schema drift. supabase/migrations/0004 creates 7 columns; TEST and PROD both carry 5 additional columns and 2 named check constraints that no repo migration creates. Repo migrations no longer reproduce live schema, which undermines the free per-PR local Supabase strategy. A full-table drift audit belongs to the governance lane.

One real ownership collision occurred and was contained: two Terra lanes initially shared a single working tree; slot 1 was moved to a dedicated git worktree and file ownership was verified with comm before opening each PR.

Second schema drift found: portfolios.line_sort_order exists on both TEST and PROD but no repo migration creates it. A building agent read the repo migrations, concluded the column was missing, and was about to disable a working feature. Read-only verification against the live database prevented that. Drift is therefore not only a tidiness problem; it causes agents to misjudge features as infeasible.

One shared TEST collision was detected and contained: the WIP guard now auto-dispatches the canonical TEST on lane transition (behaviour introduced by governance PR #166 during this run), which duplicated the session's manual dispatch on PR #169. The pending duplicate run was cancelled before it started and no manual dispatch was issued for later lane transitions.

Owner steer 2026-09-04: restore broken functionality rather than cancel it. Codified on main as docs/DELIVERY-CHAIN.md (commit cb29f973) together with the six-gate delivery chain, plus two OWNER-DECISIONS entries and cross-references from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and docs/AGENT-EXECUTION.md.

Correction issued publicly on Issue #7: campaigns was earlier escalated as an Owner decision on missing backend columns. That was inference, not observation. src/app/api/campaigns/route.ts already documents that display fields go into the content jsonb, and both POST and PUT accept it. Only participantCount is a genuine gap (no campaign_participants table and no migration carrying campaign_id anywhere in the repo); it is a derived aggregate and cannot live in content jsonb without becoming a permanently stale fake number.

Sol audit on pull/175 caught a button that would always fail: the delete action had been wired to DELETE /api/campaigns/:id, but that handler did not exist, so real mode would always return 405. Before the change it was a fake success, after it would have been a guaranteed failure; neither is a working feature. A DELETE handler was added (mirroring PUT: MANAGER role, id + tenant_id double-condition isolation, 404 without leaking existence, ENDED deletable since removal is not editing). Two tests that had locked in the absence of DELETE were removed and replaced with tests for the handler.

Five product PRs merged and Completion-Truth-verified this run: #168 3552e9d6, #169 0aca4b63, #171 42335a02, #172 be118811, #173 0173ba47. shipped_units remains 0 because AUTHENTICATED_PRODUCTION_ACCEPTED has not been performed for any of them.

The #177 canonical TEST failure demonstrated why both TEST profiles are needed and neither substitutes for the other: local isolated proves the migration itself is written correctly (fresh database, 0001 through 0076 applied in order), while canonical TEST proves the shared database's schema has actually been brought up to date. Local green plus canonical red is a coherent, informative pair, not a contradiction.

Correction issued to the Owner and to Issue #176: the initial claim that campaign settings trigger nothing at all was wrong. Birthday greetings and customer recall ARE fully implemented as real daily Vercel cron jobs (birthday-greetings at Taipei 09:00, customer-recall at 14:00) that send real LINE pushes, consume push quota, gate on features, and dedupe via last_recall_at. They are driven by tenant_settings.notify (the notification settings page), not by the campaigns page. The real problem is therefore two competing UIs for the same capability, not a missing capability, which substantially reduces the scope of #176.

pull/177 discloses that the customer source badge will show for nobody after merge, and that this is correct: the repo contains exactly one code path that inserts into customers (the manual admin POST). No LINE or public-booking auto-creation exists, so the customers page copy promising it is currently untrue. Escalated to the Owner rather than silently changing the copy or removing the badge.

pull/179 found a genuine defect beyond the wiring: the marketing page listed a COMPLETED status that the backend never writes (the real value is SENT), making that filter and label dead code. Also widened the send button to the backend's actual SENDABLE set so a failed push can be retried instead of being a dead end. The real LINE send endpoint was never invoked during construction or verification, and no integration or E2E test touches it.
